title: Composite streaming-chat service contracts: latency bands, availability targets, and phased canary gating
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Define and approve a composite service contract (SLA/SLO) for the new real-time streaming chat endpoint. This ticket formalizes latency envelopes for both time-to-first-byte (TTFB) and per-token tail behavior, availability targets, error-budget allocation, and an automated, phased canary gating plan tied to synthetic and production canary cohorts. The goal is to enable a safe rollout of streaming optimizations (KV caching changes and kernel scheduler tweaks) while keeping degradation risk small for existing customers.
background: Streaming chat changes (runtime-1.22) introduce continuous batching and a new token scheduler that reduce cost but change latency distribution for short sessions. Engineering has a draft histogram from internal perf runs; PM needs a concrete operational contract and rollout plan that ops, legal (SLA language), and SRE can sign off on.
scope:
- Define SLO metrics (TTFB, per-token p50/p95/p99) and availability by region and customer tier.
- Set monthly error budgets and burn-rate thresholds that gate rollouts.
- Specify automated canary stages and quantitative pass/fail criteria for each stage.
- Deliver monitoring queries, dashboard links, and alert conditions.
- Produce an SLA blurb for customer-facing docs (hosted tier).
out_of_scope:
- Dedicated/private contractual SLAs for enterprise customers (separate negotiation).
- Billing/price changes tied to new performance profiles.
- Implementation work for the scheduler (engineering tickets will follow).
deliverables:
- Approved SLO table and SLA paragraph for hosted streaming chat.
- Phased canary gating playbook with automated checks.
- Observability runbook: dashboard links, PromQL/LogQL examples, and alert thresholds.
- Acceptance criteria for runtime and console teams to sign off on before rollout.
success_metrics:
- No customer-visible P0 incidents attributable to runtime-1.22 during rollout.
- Error budget consumption for hosted streaming stays below 30% in first 14 days post-100% rollout.
- Latency improvement: median token latency improves by >=10% vs baseline in steady-state load tests.
- Canary false-positive rate < 2% (i.e., automated gates do not block healthy changes more than 2% of successful rollouts historically).
slo_specification:
Primary metrics (hosted, global):
- Time-to-first-byte (TTFB) for streaming start: p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 350ms, p99 <= 600ms.
- Per-token generation latency (measured per-client stream): p50 <= 15ms, p95 <= 80ms, p99 <= 220ms.
- Availability SLA (monthly uptime): 99.95% for hosted streaming endpoints (excludes planned maintenance with 48h notice).
- Error budget: 0.05% monthly availability allowance (~2.2 hours).
Notes: Percentiles measured on successful responses only; separate metric tracks token errors and model failures.
burn_rate_and_gating:
- Error-budget burn-rate windows: 1h, 6h, 24h.
- Gate thresholds:
  * Soft gate (canary advancement blocked): if 24h burn-rate > 2x baseline OR p95 latency regression > +15% vs baseline.
  * Hard gate (immediate rollback): if 1h burn-rate > 5x OR availability drops below 99.8% in any region for >15 minutes.
- Operator actions tied to gates: pause rollout, reduce traffic percentage, enable fallback model, or rollback to last healthy config.
- Escalation: SRE page if hard gate triggered; exec notify if >50% of monthly error budget consumed within 48h.
phased_rollout_plan:
Stage 0 - Synthetic canary (1 synthetic region, internal traffic): run 48h; require synthetic p95 <= baseline + 10% and no errors.
Stage 1 - Production canary (1% of traffic, geographically isolated shard): 24h; require error-budget consumption <10% of monthly budget and p95 <= baseline + 12%.
Stage 2 - Gradual ramp (10% traffic): 24h; require burn-rate <1.5x and per-token p99 within +20ms of baseline.
Stage 3 - Broad ramp (25% -> 50% over 48h): require 48h stability, error-budget consumption delta <20% from baseline.
Stage 4 - Full rollout (100%): monitor 14d; automatic rollback if at any time hard gates breach.
Each stage is automated through rollout controller with manual override option; canary cohorts include a labeled opt-in tenant set for early access.
monitoring_and_alerting:
Dashboards: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/streaming-chat/slo-overview
Key queries (examples):
- TTFB p95: sum by(region) (histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(runtime_stream_ttfb_bucket[5m])))
- Per-token p99: histogram_quantile(0.99, rate(runtime_token_latency_bucket[10m]))
- Availability: 1 - (sum(runtime_stream_errors) / sum(runtime_stream_requests)) over 24h
Alerts:
- SLO-warning (page): if 24h burn-rate > 2x OR p95 TTFB regression > +20% for 30m.
- SLO-breach (page+pager): if monthly burn-rate projected to exhaust >50% within 72h or availability <99.8% for 15m.
- Canary-block (ticket to rollout owner + slack): if stage gate conditions fail.
acceptance_criteria: SLO table reviewed and approved by SRE, Legal (SLA language), Runtime, and PM.
Automated canary pipeline configured with the gating thresholds above and verified in staging.
Dashboards and alerts created and validated with sample traffic; alert runbook populated.
Rollout controller implements stage percentages and automatic rollback triggers; manual override documented.
A short customer-facing SLA blurb drafted and reviewed by legal and growth for hosted users.

risks_and_mitigations:
Risks: latent regional network spikes could inflate p99s and cause unnecessary rollbacks; synthetic traffic may not mirror production patterns for multi-tenant workloads.
Mitigations: require both synthetic AND production canary passes before advancing; include regional holdback in canary to detect network-specific regressions; fallback policy to serve non-streaming (blocking) responses for high-latency tenants to preserve correctness.
